edits.target: Give the bare name ('Ronald Reagan'), not the event, the place or the date.
edits.content: - Part-of-name clues ('First name of the man elected chancellor of a reunified Germany in 1990', 'Last name of...', 'Surname of...', 'Initials of...'): first identify the person from the passages (Helmut Kohl), then output ONLY the requested part ('Helmut'). Do not give the full name, a title, or a group label.

edits.target: - A word in quotation marks inside the clue (a 'drag', a nickname) is usually a pun or hint tied to the answer. Look for passages where that word appears next to a candidate and answer with that candidate.
edits.content:
- When the quoted word is itself a generic head noun right after 'this' ('Fog forms when air cools to this "point"', 'this "bubble"'), it is the head of a standard compound that the passages repeat ('dew point'). Answer with the full compound, keeping the quoted word. Do not strip it to the bare modifier ('dew'). This is the head-noun exception to the delete-clue-words test, not an echo error.
- Short descriptor-plus-quote clues ('A comedienne: "Ball of Fire"') ask for the person, work or thing that the quoted phrase points to. The phrase may contain the answer's own name ('Ball' -> 'Lucille Ball') or be her known nickname. Pick the candidate whose name or alias is inside the phrase AND who fits the descriptor. A film or work that merely shares the title (such as a different actress who starred in Ball of Fire) is not the answer. Never answer with the quoted phrase itself. This works even when an archive snippet stops right after the clue.
- Grammar-role clues ('The adverb in "think fast"', 'the verb in ...', 'the noun in ...') are the one case where the answer IS a word from the clue (an explicit exception to the echo guard). Pick the single word inside the quoted phrase that has the named part of speech ('fast'), not a synonym ('quickly') and not the whole phrase. Passages that discuss the phrase (dictionary, grammar-forum or quiz-archive pages) confirm which word.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - ECHO GUARD: after drafting an answer, compare it with the clue text. If your candidate (or a longer form of it) is a name, place or word the clue itself states, reject it: the clue names anchors, not the answer. 'In 1579 this English circumnavigator put the Golden Hind in for repairs at an inlet north of San Francisco' -> the circumnavigator (Drake), not 'San Francisco'. 'A "letter to" this person, like Ben Bradlee, ...' -> 'like X' gives an example of the role, so answer the role ('The editor'), not X. 'The university of this U.S. territory is home to the Micronesian Area Research Center' -> 'Guam', not 'University of Guam' (the pattern 'the <thing> of this <noun>' asks for the <noun> alone). 'The alliance of these Chinese businesses became a civil rights group' -> 'laundries', the plural members the pointer stands for, not the alliance's own name. A page or archive CATEGORY word ('SORRY YOU'RE POOR') is not the answer either. (The only exceptions are the grammar-role clues and the quoted generic head-noun clues described below.)
